title: Crispy Cheese Cloud Buns
creator: Steak & Butter Gal
instructions: Heat an air fryer to 175°C, or an oven to 200°C, and line the tray with parchment.
Whip the egg whites with a pinch of salt until they hold stiff peaks.
Fold the grated cheese through gently in two additions so the mixture stays airy.
Spoon into four thick bun-sized rounds and flatten only slightly.
Air-fry for 12-14 minutes, or bake about 12 minutes, until browned, dry on the surface and firm enough to lift.
Cool for a few minutes before filling; toast the cut side in butter for an even crisper burger bun.
doneness: Golden, set through the centre and firm enough to hold a burger without collapsing.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days between parchment.
strictNote: The indexed Instagram version uses garlic powder and other seasonings; this strict version keeps only egg white, cheese and salt.

title: Cast-Iron Bacon Cheeseburger Egg Skillet
creator: Stephanie | Carnivore Meals
ingredients: 4 rashers bacon with no sugar fillers
instructions: Cook the bacon in butter over medium heat until browned and crisp; leave the rendered fat in the cast-iron pan.
Add the beef mince, press it into a broad layer and leave it untouched for 2-3 minutes so the underside develops a dark crust.
Break the beef into chunky pieces, salt it and cook until nearly done.
Scatter the bacon and cheddar over the beef, letting some cheese touch the bare pan so it fries into crisp edges.
Make four small gaps, crack in the eggs, cover, then lower or switch off the heat and let the residual heat set the whites.
Serve straight from the skillet with the crisp cheese pieces scraped from the bottom.
doneness: Egg whites set, beef safely cooked and cheese crisp around the edges.
storage: The beef-and-bacon base keeps 3-4 days refrigerated.
reheat: Reheat the base in a skillet and add fresh cheese and eggs at the end.

title: Beef & Turkey Meatza with Cheese
creator: Cookingalongwithme
ingredients: 150 g plain pepperoni with no sugar/starch
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and line a large sheet pan with parchment.
Mix the beef and turkey with salt just until combined, then press into an even meat crust about 1-1.5 cm thick.
Bake for 15-18 minutes until the meat contracts and releases liquid.
Drain excess liquid and fat carefully.
Cover with pepperoni, mozzarella or Muenster, and parmesan.
Bake another 8-12 minutes until fully cooked and bubbling; broil briefly if you want browned cheese edges.
Rest 5 minutes before slicing so the meat crust holds together.
doneness: Firm meat base that lifts in slices with bubbling, browned cheese.
storage: Refrigerate 4 days or freeze individual cooked slices.
reheat: Air-fry or oven-reheat at 180°C until hot and crisp at the edges.
strictNote: The Instagram version includes tomato sauce, red pepper, basil and seasonings; this version removes them.

title: Butter-Basted Filet & Lobster Surf and Turf
creator: Cookingalongwithme
instructions: Pat the steaks dry, salt them and let them lose some fridge chill while you prepare the lobster.
Cut down the top of each lobster shell with kitchen scissors, loosen the meat and lift it onto the shell.
Brush the lobster generously with melted butter and salt.
Sear the filets in a very hot heavy pan for about 2-3 minutes per side, then lower the heat and baste with butter until they reach your preferred doneness.
Rest the steaks for 5-8 minutes.
Broil the lobster under high heat until opaque, firm but still juicy; start checking at roughly one minute per ounce of tail weight.
Serve together and spoon the hot butter over the lobster.
doneness: Lobster opaque and tender; steak at your preferred safe internal temperature after resting.
storage: Best fresh; refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days.
reheat: Warm gently in butter so the lobster does not become rubbery.
strictNote: The Instagram version flavours the butter with lemon, garlic and spices; this version uses butter and salt only.

title: Half-Pound Shrimp & Blue Cheese Burger
creator: KETO CARNIVORE BBQ
instructions: Form the beef into one loose half-pound patty and salt both sides.
Sear in a hot heavy skillet or on a grill until a dark crust develops, then flip and finish to your preferred safe doneness.
Rest the burger for 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, sear the shrimp in butter for roughly 1-2 minutes per side until just opaque.
Add blue cheese to the hot burger and cover briefly if you want it softer.
Pile the shrimp over the cheese and spoon over the browned butter from the seafood pan.
Serve bunless or inside a strict carnivore bun.
doneness: Burger browned and safely cooked; shrimp opaque but still tender.
reheat: Reheat the burger in a skillet and warm the shrimp very briefly before serving.
strictNote: The Instagram post references seasoning blends; this strict version uses salt only.

title: Egg-Yolk Waffle Burger Buns
creator: Sarah Kleiner / Carnivore Yogi
ingredients: 1 tbsp bacon grease, tallow or melted butter
instructions: Preheat a mini waffle iron and grease it lightly with bacon fat or tallow.
Whisk the yolks, animal fat and a pinch of salt until glossy and fully combined.
Pour enough mixture into the iron to cover the grid without flooding the edges.
Cook until steam slows and the waffle lifts cleanly, usually 3-5 minutes depending on the iron.
Cool for one minute so it firms up.
Use two small waffles as a burger bun, or fill them with sausage, bacon and cheese for breakfast.
doneness: Set, pliable and lightly browned with no wet yolk in the centre.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days between parchment.
reheat: Reheat in the waffle iron for 1-2 minutes.
strictNote: This is a strict adaptation of an Instagram-attributed egg-yolk waffle idea; some published versions add baking powder.
